description:
addressbook.rs:349 inside the onSuccessSetIsDefault block:

    Ok(Some(obj)) => {
        mutated = true;
        updated.insert(
            target_id.to_string(),
            serde_json::to_value(&obj).unwrap_or(Value::Null),
        );

The unwrap_or(Value::Null) here is inconsistent with every other to_value call in this file. The same pattern at addressbook.rs:159-160, 214-215, card.rs:131-132, 187-188 uses:

    serde_json::to_value(&obj).expect("derive(Serialize) on plain data is infallible")

(documented in helpers.rs:14-19 as the workspace policy for "Serialize-derive on plain data cannot fail"). The .unwrap_or(Value::Null) at line 349 diverges from this policy without a comment explaining why.

Three possibilities:
  1. Intentional: the author wanted soft-failure here because §2.3 says "errors are silently ignored" — but §2.3 is about errors from the update_object backend call, not about serialization of the result. Silently producing Value::Null in the response for a successful update is wrong.
  2. Unintentional: cargo-culted-wrong from another spot; should be .expect to match the file's convention.
  3. Defensive: the AddressBook type contains a field with non-string map keys that serde_json cannot serialize — but AddressBook is derive-Serialize on plain data per the workspace pattern.

The idiomatic Rust answer is to match the file's convention: either .expect everywhere (and document the invariant once) or .map_err everywhere (and propagate). Mixing the two is a cargo-cult smell.

Note line 367 uses `if let Ok(v) = serde_json::to_value(&book) { updated.insert(book_id.to_string(), v); }` — yet a third pattern in the same file. Three different serializations of the same shape of data, three different error handlers.
title: addressbook.rs:349 serde_json::to_value(&obj).unwrap_or(Value::Null) silently drops post-update serialize error
